title: Meru voice pack
order: script order; lines sharing a 'scene' play one after another

items.text: You have been holding that piece a while now.
I am thinking about it.
You are hoping about it.
At my level those are the same thing.
He is losing again. He always loses.
There. That took you long enough.
I had to be SURE.
You were sure four moves ago.
Being sure early is exactly how I lose.
It is also how he wins. Watch.
Jump it. Go on, jump it.
That is a trap and you know it.
Everything is a trap with you.
And yet here we are, dead even.
Crown that one. You have earned it.
I do know the rules, thank you.
You forgot them entirely on Tuesday.
On Tuesday I was being GENEROUS.
Serve it properly this time.
That one WAS properly!
That was a tap and you know it.
It went all the way round twice!
My arm is going to come off.
Then stop swinging quite so hard.
Swinging hard is the only part I am good at.
Is anyone else's back doing this?
Mine has done that for eleven years.
Breathe out on the way DOWN.
I am breathing out on the way down.
He says it gets easier eventually.
He says that to everybody, every week.
It did get easier, though. Honestly.
You absolute traitor.
Your music is lovely. At six in the morning.
Six is when I am awake!
So is the entire tower now.
Did you get the letter about the roof?
I got three of them.
Did any of them actually say anything?
They said there would be a letter.
You are watering that plant again.
It is thriving!
It is dripping on my washing.
Something went under the ferry this morning.
Something always goes under the ferry.
This one was BIG.
Watch this one. Watch it.
I have watched eleven of these.
This one is DIFFERENT.
It is in the gutter, Dash.
Start left of centre and let it drift in.
That is Gale's advice.
Gale gives very good advice.
Gale has never once taken it.
Table four, no onions.
Table four never wants onions.
Then why must I say it every time?
Because one day they will want onions.
Order up! Hot plate!
It is always a hot plate.
And you always put your thumb in it.
Best of three. Come on.
That already was best of three.
Then best of FIVE.
I have got all afternoon.
You are getting much better, you know.
Please do not do that.
Do what?
Be KIND about it.
This one is warm. I can feel it.
They are all warm to you.
One more pull and I am done.
That is what warm MEANS.
I am up. I am properly up.
Then walk away from it.
In a minute. One minute.
That is the whole trick of this room.
Blow on them for luck. Go on.
I am not allowed to do that.
Who on earth is going to know?
The cameras. The boss. Everybody.
New shooter. Place your bets.
Same bet as last time, exactly.
Last time did not go well for you.
Last time was RESEARCH.
Something strong and something small.
Those are usually the same order.
Tonight they are not.
How has the wheel been treating you?
The wheel has been honest.
That is not a yes.
No. It is not a yes.
Did you see the lake today?
I saw the lake.
Something went under the ferry!
Something always goes under the ferry.
It is your round, Ziggy.
It is always my round.
You keep saying that, and it keeps being true.
Double top. Watch this.
I am carrying four plates.
Then listen for it!
I heard the WALL, Flick.
Eat something before you throw.
Food makes my arm heavy.
So does beer.
Beer makes my arm BRAVE.
I was near the relic. Near is not stealing.
You were holding it in both paws.
Holding is only near, with hands.
The Chief says Thursday.
The Chief said Thursday last Thursday.
Then we are owed one.
Forty minutes I have sat on this bench.
I live on this bench.
Why would you do that?
Warmest room in town.
They have lost my paperwork again.
What paperwork?
That is exactly my point.
Another one going down for pearls.
They never check the depth first.
The Prince did not check the depth.
And look how that turned out.
Tide turns in about an hour.
Should we say something to him?
We are saying something. Loudly.
You cut the second buoy.
I rounded the second buoy.
You went straight THROUGH it.
He did go through it.
Rematch. Right now.
My engine is still smoking.
Then I win by default.
That is not how winning works.
You rolled that one soft.
I rolled that one FAST.
I heard it coming from the door.
Then you should have stopped it.
Thirty one pages in one hour.
Reading is not a sport.
Say that to me at the regionals.
Play the one from yesterday.
I have never played the same thing twice.
Then play it wrong again.
What is it going to be this time?
A fox. Or possibly a boat.
Which of the two?
It will tell me when it is ready.
Mine is bigger than your whole book.
Mine fits in one pocket.
Mine can be read from the DOOR.
Town Square platform! Mind the doors!
Town Square. Every line stops here and every fox is in a hurry.
One way or return. Decide before you reach the window.
Market Plaza! Mind your baskets!
Market Plaza. I know what every trader is carrying before they tell me.
Go early for fruit. Go late for a bargain. Never go at noon.
Lakeside! Mind the gap and mind the gulls!
Lakeside. The gulls have learned to open a paper bag.
If the water is flat, the ferry runs. If it is not, it does not.
Crestview! Top of the climb!
Crestview. Highest platform on the loop, and I keep it swept.
Stand at the end there before you board. Best view in Meru, free.
Arena Road! Have your tickets ready!
Arena Road. Quiet six days a week, then a thousand foxes at once.
Going up is easy. Coming back down, everybody wants the same train.
Castle Path. Mind the step.
Castle Path. Four trains a day and most of them leave empty.
The foxes who get off here were sent for. That is the whole platform.
Ruins Road! Last stop west!
Ruins Road. Last stop west, and the last light for a long while.
Be back on this platform before dark. I will not wait and the train will not either.
Spire station! Hold your hat!
Spire. The wind comes straight down the tower and takes anything loose.
Machines going up, machines coming down. I stopped counting them.
Foxes of Meru! Up here, if you can spare me!
Not for long. I know there is a match at the stadium.
You want to be in the stands for the first serve. So do I.
I will be quick.
Look up. Go on, properly. Past the roofs, past the gold.
Before any fox wrote anything down, we did not walk. We flew.
It is in the scrolls in that library, and the library has never lied to us.
There was an age when foxes crossed the dark as balls of light.
And the stars were not scenery. They were a ROAD.
And the road is still open. You have seen the Gate.
You know what it is. A hole in the sky with a turnstile on it.
There are worlds beyond this one. More than the church has names for.
Every one of them has a sky.
And under every sky tonight somebody stands exactly where you stand.
Wondering exactly what you are wondering.
Now. The vein.
The stone in that mountain is light that has been sitting still four hundred years.
It is sacred. It is not a price.
Cut it for a lamp in a hut. Cut it for the glass over the gorge.
Cut it so a cleric can read after dark, and the Gate keeps.
But cut it for GAIN, and I promise you, it goes dark in the hand.
And so do you.
The same goes for the water. The road. The trees standing either side of it.
We did not make this place. We were put into it.
And we have been loud guests.
And play. I mean that. It is doctrine, not a kindness.
We have hit a ball across a net on this planet for a century.
Without once agreeing to count the points!
And we are the happiest world through that Gate.
A fox at play is a fox telling the truth.
One more thing, and then go.
There is a homeworld. It is called Earth.
Every fox here came from it, and every fox here returns to it.
And not as a passenger.
As a light.
So. Respect the stone. Respect the water.
Be kind, be loud, and be on time for the first serve.
The Gate keeps. Go and play.
Truck on land, boat on water!
Truck on land, boat on water. Same rule for both, get there FIRST.
Hold on to something. I do not do slow.
Half of this town is wood. All of the lake is water.
The siren is my favourite part. The Chief says it should not be.
Three paws on the rungs! Always three!
Forty feet, wind, smoke, up there I am fine. Down here I struggle.
Down here foxes TALK to me. Much worse than smoke.
Raise it slow. Lock it. Then climb. Never in another order.
Pass me that rope on your way past.
Sorry! Did I get you?
Hose rule one is point it AWAY from your friends.
I am still working on rule one.
Sweep side to side, low, at the flames. Never at the smoke.
I get everyone. It is a gift. Nobody wants it.
Stand clear of me. I mean that kindly.
Mind the hoses! Spritz leaves them everywhere!
Mind the hoses. Spritz leaves them everywhere. I am Chief Ember.
Back again. The bell has been quiet. Let us keep it that way.
Boots by the door. Then we talk.
Good timing. Something always starts burning when I sit down.
Aim at the BASE of a fire, never at the smoke.
On a ladder, three paws on the rungs. Always three.
A hydrant you never checked is a hydrant that will not work.
Count your crew in, and then count them out again.
A cat comes down when it wants to. Help it want to.
Clean work. Everyone came home. That is the only score that counts.
Not bad. Hang the gear back where you found it.
That was textbook. I will put your name on the board.
Stay clear of the smoke. And of Spritz.
All three lanes open! Shoes on the rack!
All three lanes are open and not one of them costs a coin.
Put me on a lane.
Shoes are on the rack behind me. Take a pair, bring them back.
That is the whole arrangement.
Tell me who is worth bowling against.
ROOK at the table bowls a hundred and forty seven, near enough every week.
Gale down at lane one has been trying to beat him since the spring.
Ask him how it is going. Go on.
And Nera at the racks holds the house. She will say it was luck.
It was not.
I want to know why they are free.
King Might had them laid the year the gates woke.
He said a city that only knows how to fight forgets how to be a city.
Show me what else is in here.
Two boards on the north wall, and they are properly weighted.
Not like the tavern's, which lean left and always have.
And the jukebox by the east wall. Put something on.
The quiet in here gets loud.
I will come back for a lane.
Bring the shoes back.
Do not ask me how it is going!
Forty one weeks against ROOK. Forty one.
Tell me what he does differently.
Nothing! That is the horror of it.
Same line, same speed, same little nod before he lets go.
No spin, no risk, no flair.
Give me some advice for the lanes.
Start left of centre and let it drift in.
And do not chase a strike on the second ball.
A spare counts. A gutter counts for nothing.
I have seen you throw. It is a good ball.
I throw a BEAUTIFUL ball. Absolutely beautiful.
Then I throw a gutter, and he throws his hundred and forty seventh pin.
And we go home.
I will leave you to it.
Advice I give freely and have never once taken.
Two hundred and twelve! Four years ago!
Two hundred and twelve. Lane two, a Tuesday, nobody in but Mott.
I am going to beat that number.
Every chance. It is a good number, not a great one.
Go on. I would rather lose it to somebody than sit on it.
Tell me if you bowl against Rook.
No. Rook bowls against the pins and Gale bowls against Rook.
Neither of them is having any fun at all.
I want to know how close you have come since.
Not within thirty of it. I do not mind. It happened.
Thank you for the number.
Pick a ball, throw it badly, go home. That is the whole sport.
Same table. Same ball. Every week.
Eleven years, same table, same fourteen pounds of ball.
Gale says you never miss.
A hundred and forty seven. Occasionally four less.
Once a hundred and fifty one, which unsettled me for a month.
I would want to do better than that.
Nera has the house and she is welcome to it.
Chasing a number is how Gale ended up like Gale.
Tell me which lane to take.
The middle one. It runs true.
I will try the middle lane.
A lane asks the same question ten times and does not care about yesterday.
What year is it?
I appear to have mislaid a year. Possibly several.
Tell me who you are looking for.
A young fox. Red bodywarmer. Talks fast, thinks faster.
He has a habit of arriving before he has left.
Somebody else asked me that today.
Somebody ELSE? Who else has asked you that.
No. No, do not answer that.
The less I know, the less there is to go wrong. Where was I.
I will keep an eye out for him.
If you see him, tell him nothing about his own future.
NOTHING. Not the weather.
I will leave you to your notes.
Yes. Yes. Mind the step on your way out. Or do not.
Stay behind me, Ruler.
The perimeter is tense. Luxor's guards are tracking us with heavy scanners.
Tell me whether we are safe in here.
My shielding arrays will absorb any kinetic fire.
Stay behind me and nothing reaches you.
I want to know what those guards are carrying.
Their sidearms carry refined God rock gems.
The energy signatures are astronomical. Do not provoke them.
Then we watch and we say nothing.
Correct, Ruler. I will hold this door until you are finished.
Stay close tonight.
I have never once been further than four paces.
Boards are free! Jukebox takes no coin!
We pour, we feed you, and the boards on the wall cost nothing.
Yes. Put me to work.
Apron on. Pull the pints level and carry three at a time, not four.
Four is how we lose glasses.
Tell me about the boards.
They lean LEFT. Everyone says so and nobody has straightened them.
Mott down at the lanes brings it up every single week.
I want to know who drinks in here.
A protector who will not sit down. A scientist who has lost a year.
And Ziggy, who has seen something in the lake again.
Goodbye for now.
Mind the darts on your way past Flick.
Great burgers! Super fun to make!
We have great burgers here, and we are looking for good staff.
Sounds tasty. Put me to work.
Apron on. Ticket rail is above the grill.
Read it before you touch anything.
Teach me how to make burgers.
Seven things, in order, and the ticket tells you all seven.
Sear the patty and FLIP it so both sides match.
Cheese goes on before it comes off the heat, or it sits there cold.
Then sauce, then dress the bun with only what the ticket asks for.
Only what it asks for.
Chop the side, fry it GOLDEN, slide the cup under the right tap.
Tell me how you got into this.
I cooked for the barracks. Two hundred foxes, twice a day.
Not one of them ever said a word about it.
So I put a griddle on a cart at the arena gate. Sold out before the second bout.
The Tavern let me build onto their east wall for a cut of it.
Best deal either of us ever made. They get the trade, I get the wall.
Maybe later.
Grill stays hot. Come back when you are hungry, or when you are broke.
What year is it?
Never mind. Forget I asked. I ask everyone.
Tell me why you want to know.
I would rather not say it out loud in a diner.
If you meet a confused scientist, tell him Michael Jay is here.
I have met a confused scientist.
Then do NOT tell me what he said.
Tell him where I am. Tell him nothing else at all.
I will pass it on.
Good. And the burgers really are worth it.
You just missed it!
Prince Max was diving right there for hull pearls. You just missed it.
Tell me what happened to him.
He woke the sea monster. Nelly.
Prince Max fled fast. Said he was off to the Tavern.
To calm his nerves, he said.
I want to know about these pearls.
Hull pearls sit deep, under the old boats on the bottom.
Which is also where Nelly sits. Nobody has ever found one and been pleased.
Tell me about the monster.
Old. Long. Asleep until this morning.
I have fished this water thirty years and never seen her move.
Then I am going to the Tavern.
Go quickly. And do not go in the water on the way.
Boats for hire! Rods included!
Boats for hire, rods included, and I will not ask what you catch.
Yes. Put me to work.
Take the small boat. Hold to load the cast, let go when it feels long.
Wait for the line to PULL before you strike. That is the whole of it.
Tell me where the fish are.
Deep off the rocks in the morning. In the reeds by the afternoon.
Never both on the same day, and I have never worked out why.
I heard something woke up out there.
I heard it too. I have moved my lines closer in.
Goodbye for now.
Bring the rod back and we are square.
Garden Island! Mind your step aboard!
Garden Island and back. We go when the water is flat and not before.
Take me across.
Aboard then. Sit where you like, hold on where you must.
Tell me what is worth seeing over there.
Towers, money and a gallery. The island is fancy and knows it.
Something went under this boat this morning. I have not mentioned it.
Another time.
We run till dusk. After that the water gets opinions.
Mind the gap! Both feet!
Out here! I cannot make it back!
My boat! Somebody, my boat!
Another traveller drawn to the old stones.
Few climb this path now. Come closer, and mind the plinths.
Tell me about the ruins ahead.
Older than the eight gates themselves.
When the centre hub was split, a shard fell here.
This temple grew around it. The builders are long gone.
Their work still hums.
I am going inside.
Then you should know the lower halls flooded generations ago.
The dark took what the water did not.
Bats, rats and worse nest down there. Carry light, keep your blade close.
Do NOT trust the still water.
Tell me why the ruins matter now.
A piece of the broken centre gate sleeps inside.
The very fragment Luxor would kill to hold.
Whoever holds it holds a key to the gates.
I will bring you anything old I find.
I pay full worth. No shopkeeper's half.
Goodbye for now.
Tread carefully. The old stones remember everything.
Ruins road! Last light for a long while!
West is the ruins. Past them the desert, and past that nothing with a name.
Tell me what I should know.
The site is safe enough in daylight. What is UNDER it is not.
The way under is a stair in the middle of the floor.
Most foxes find it with their ankles.
I want to know who keeps the museum.
The Sage, up the path. He pays full worth for anything old.
He is the only reason this road gets swept.
I am heading up.
Be back past me before dark.
Field is shut! No permits today!
No permit today, friend. The field is shut.
Tell me why. There is nobody out here.
That is exactly why. They are all at the ARENA.
King Might is hosting his own birthday tournament.
Every digger went to watch?
Every fox worth the name. I would be there too.
Then I will come back after.
Come back when the competition is done. Then I will stamp you one.
Goodbye for now.
Shovels are where you left them.
Sit. The ball is not quiet tonight.
I see what is already HERE. Most foxes simply have not looked yet.
Tell me what I have not looked at.
Something is lost. Not a thing. A someone.
And the whole town is about to notice at once.
You will be the one who finds him.
That is not a kindness. It is just true.
Then I will go and learn his name.
Come back when you know it, and I will tell you where to walk.
You carry a name that is not yours.
Max. Everyone is saying it. You brought it in with you.
Tell me where he is.
I know where he WAS, and that is how you find anyone.
The ball is wet. Deep water, south of the square.
And something old asleep under it.
Then I am going to the lake.
Find the one who was watching when it woke.
The ball still tastes of the water.
Ah. You have been to the water already. I can taste it in here.
He was not there.
No. He RAN from there, with his heart up in his throat.
A frightened fox does not go home, child. He goes where the drink is.
Then I will try the Tavern.
Ask the regulars. All of them. One of them watched him leave.
You have been drinking with talkers. Good.
You have been drinking with talkers. Good. Now look.
Tell me what you see.
Stone. Broken stone, west of the square, older than the King.
And a stair. Going down, where a stair has no business going.
He is under it. He is not alone under it.
Then I will go down it.
Take something that BITES.
The cage is open. I saw the bar swing.
The cage is OPEN. I saw the bar swing from this chair.
Then I do not understand why he is still down there.
Because nobody has asked him.
Go back down the stair. Say the words out loud. He will follow.
I will say them.
Out loud, child. Not in your head.
Two sets of paws came through my door.
Two sets of paws came through my door. Only one of you is lost now.
I did not think you could hear that.
I can hear a great deal. Take him to his FATHER. Straight there.
Do not stop to dig. Do not stop to gamble.
The dunes will still be dunes tomorrow.
Straight to the castle, then.
Straight there. I will know if you wander.
I felt the room lighten when you walked in.
The lost is found. I felt the room lighten when you walked in.
Then it is over.
No, child. That was the EASY thing.
Prepare for great trials.
Iron is coming down out of the dark.
And it does not care whose birthday it is.
Tell me what to do with that.
Eat. Sharpen something. Stay near the KING.
Sit. The ball has gone quiet.
Sit. The ball has gone QUIET for the first time in a long while.
Tell me whether that is good.
It is rare. A sky with nothing falling out of it.
You did that. Not the King. Not the fleet. You.
Then I will go and be young somewhere.
Go and be young somewhere. The eighth gate will keep.
Fish! Nobody else thought of fish!
Everyone up here is selling pie and beer. I walk down and buy fish.
Tell me if that works.
It works on the FIGHTERS. They will not eat pastry before a bout.
Sits on you, they say. So they come to me and pay whatever I ask.
That is a good trick.
It is the whole trick of a fight day.
Sell to the ones who cannot eat what everybody else is eating.
Goodbye for now.
Eat before you go up. Not pastry.
Take one! Nobody buys fruit today!
Whatever the orchard gave me. Take one. No, take one, I mean it.
Tell me what they do buy.
Pies and beer and little red flags.
Nobody comes to an arena to eat sensibly.
This basket has been here a while.
My grandmother sold out of this same basket.
Back when the King's grandfather held the settlings, and there was no wall.
I would like to know if it was better then.
It was quieter. Two foxes, one argument, everybody home by supper.
Now they build things that do not bleed and we call that progress.
Goodbye for now.
Take an apple. Go on.
Ribbons! Ribbons for the card!
There is always a fight on. Whether there is a TOURNAMENT is the question.
Tell me how many you have seen.
Since I was a kit. My mother sold ribbons on this ground.
I stood on a crate to watch over the heads.
Tell me what happens in there.
Three rounds, always three. Laser gun, then staff, then sword.
And they get CLOSER to you every round. That is the joke of it.
By the end there is nothing between you and them.
I want to know the best you ever saw.
A quiet one. Never gave a name.
Went through all three without a mark and left before the speech.
Goodbye for now.
Take a red one. Red is lucky and I have too many.
Odds! Odds on any fox you like!
I have money on EVERYTHING. That is the trade.
Give me the odds on me.
Ha! Long. No offence, they are long on everybody.
The drones take the first round and most foxes never see the second.
Tell me what nobody bets on.
It is not the sword round that finishes people. It is the STAFF.
Everybody trains for the blade and nobody trains for the pole.
Noted. I will remember that.
Noted, he says. Come back and tell me if I was right.
Pies! Hot, and I have plenty!
Quiet as a grave until the horn goes. Then a hundred foxes at once.
You must hear a lot, standing here.
I hear all of it. Who is fighting, who is frightened.
Who has told their family they are only coming to watch.
Tell me what you hear most.
Everybody who walks up that road is sure they have a PLAN.
Nobody who walks back down says the plan survived.
Then I will take a pie.
Eat something first. That is better advice than most you will get.
Five at once! Watch the middle one!
Five, when there is a crowd. Four, when I have had a drink.
Tell me if you work the tournaments.
I work the QUEUE. Nobody watches a juggler once the gate is open.
They watch the gate. So I get them while they are still waiting.
Twenty years here. You must see patterns.
You can pick the ones who will do well.
They are the QUIET ones.
The loud ones are talking themselves into it.
The quiet ones decided at home.
Goodbye for now.
Watch this one! No, watch it!
Flowers. For the gate, not the arena.
For the GATE, not the arena. There is a stone in the tunnel wall.
Tell me whose names are on it.
Everyone who did not walk back out.
It is a short list now. They changed the rules after the settlings.
First blood and done.
Somebody you knew is on it.
My brother, from before that.
He was very fast and not very careful. One of those is enough.
I am sorry.
Be CAREFUL instead. That is worth more to me than being sorry.
I will be careful.
Take one for the stone on your way through.
Older than the wall, all of this!
Older than the wall round it. This was a threshing floor.
Tell me about a threshing floor.
Flat, hard, and big enough for the whole valley to stand on.
When the harvests failed the floor stayed.
And foxes being foxes, they found another use for a flat place.
Tell me what the first bouts were like.
Settlings. Two families, one argument, no blades.
You went until one of you sat down.
King Might's grandfather put the wall up, and the rest followed the wall.
I want to know about the eight gates.
Ah. A longer story than a stallholder tells for free.
But look at the medallion on the road, and COUNT the points.
I will count them.
Everyone walks over it. Nobody looks down.
Eleven bouts and a closer!
The card. Eleven bouts and a closer, and I have read it four times.
Tell me what you are looking for.
A name I know. There never is one.
They put the strangers first, and the strangers are the ones who last.
Tell me the word on this season.
There is an OUTSIDER on it. No house, no trainer, walked in off the road.
And I have got a copper on him, which my wife does not know about.
Do not tell her. She runs the fruit stall.
Your secret is safe.
Good fox. Good fox.
I came to watch. I have watched.
I came to watch. I have watched. I am not sure I want more.
Tell me what is so bad.
The DRONES are the worst of it.
They do not tire, they do not flinch, and they do not care who you are.
Six of them, and they come at you all at once.
Tell me where they come from.
They say the King builds them himself.
I do not know if that makes it better or worse.
Somebody has to go in.
Somebody does. I just hope it is somebody who comes back out.
Not everyone has.
Goodbye for now.
Sit with me a while if you change your mind.
This is the way to the way in!
This is the way to the way in. The gate is further up the road.
Tell me what happens at the gate.
The fox holding it asks a question you want an answer to beforehand.
Whether you are READY. Say yes and you are on the card.
Say anything else at all and you are walking back down the carpet.
I want to know how long foxes take to decide.
I have watched one stand on that spot and think about it for an hour.
Nobody minds. Nobody forgets, either.
Then I will think about it on the way up.
Most do.
Up and back. Four hundred paces each way!
Up and back. Four hundred paces each way, and I have counted them.
